subject: physics
title: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.q: Work function of the metal is
options: Maximum possible energy acquired by an electron
Minimum energy required by an electron to just eject from metal surface
Maximum energy which is given to electron to move out of metal surface
questions.explanation: The work function is defined as the minimum energy needed to just free an electron from a metal's surface.

questions.q: Variation of photoelectric current with anode potential is shown below. Choose the correct option (V$_0$ = stopping potential). [Figure: four current vs anode-potential graphs; Graph-I rises from a negative anode potential V$_0$ and saturates to a constant value; Graph-II is a straight line passing through V$_0$; Graph-III is a straight line decreasing to V$_0$; Graph-IV is an increasing exponential-like curve from V$_0$]
questions.explanation: Photoelectric current increases with anode potential and saturates at a maximum value once all emitted photoelectrons are collected, becoming zero at the stopping potential V$_0$ — this is the shape of Graph-I.

questions.q: If we consider an electron and a photon of same de-Broglie wavelength, then they will have same
questions.explanation: de Broglie wavelength $\lambda=h/p$ depends only on momentum, so equal wavelength implies equal momentum for both the electron and the photon.

questions.q: The anode voltage of a photocell is kept fixed. The frequency of the light falling on the cathode is gradually increased. Then the correct graph which shows the variation of photo current I with the frequency ν of incident light is
options: I zero till $\nu_0$ then jumping to a constant value (graph 2)
questions.explanation: For fixed intensity and anode voltage, photocurrent is zero below the threshold frequency $\nu_0$ and then jumps to a steady value independent of further increase in frequency, as shown in graph 2.

questions.q: Light of energy E falls normally on a metal of work function $\dfrac{E}{3}$. The kinetic energies (K) of the photo electrons are
questions.explanation: Maximum kinetic energy $=E-W_0=E-\dfrac{E}{3}=\dfrac{2E}{3}$; since photoelectrons can lose energy before emission, K ranges from 0 up to $\dfrac{2E}{3}$.

questions.q: The photoelectric work function for photo metal is 2.4 eV. Among the four wavelengths, the wavelength of light for which photo-emission does not take place is
questions.explanation: Threshold wavelength $\lambda_0=\dfrac{1240}{2.4}\approx517\,nm$; photoemission occurs only for $\lambda\le\lambda_0$, so at 700 nm (longer wavelength, lower photon energy) it does not take place.

questions.q: In an experiment to study photo-electric effect the observed variation of stopping potential with frequency of incident radiation is as shown in the figure [straight line graph of stopping potential V$_0$ vs frequency $\nu$, cutting the frequency axis at $\nu_0$ and rising linearly beyond it]. The slope and y-intercept respectively are
questions.explanation: From eV$_0$=h\nu−φ, V$_0$=(h/e)υ−φ/e; slope = h/e, and since V$_0$=0 at υ=υ$_0$, the y-intercept (extrapolated to υ=0) is −hυ$_0$/e.

questions.q: A 60 W source emits monochromatic light of wavelength 662.5 nm. The number of photons emitted per second is
In a photo electric experiment, if both the intensity and frequency of the incident light are doubled, then the saturation photo electric current
questions.explanation: Saturation photocurrent depends only on the number of photons incident per second, i.e. on intensity; doubling the intensity doubles the saturation current (frequency does not affect it).

questions.q: The kinetic energy of the photoelectrons increases by 0.52 eV when the wavelength of the incident light is changed from 500 nm to another wavelength which is approximately
questions.explanation: $E_{500}=1240/500=2.48$ eV. Since KE increases, the new photon energy is $2.48+0.52=3.00$ eV, giving $\lambda=1240/3.00\approx400$ nm.

questions.q: The de-Broglie wavelength of a particle of kinetic energy 'K' is $\lambda$; the wavelength of the particle, if its kinetic energy is $\dfrac{K}{4}$ is
questions.explanation: $\lambda \propto 1/\sqrt{K}$; reducing K to K/4 increases $\lambda$ by a factor of $\sqrt{4}=2$, so the new wavelength is $2\lambda$.

questions.q: The work function of a metal is 1eV. Light of wavelength 3000A° is incident on this metal surface. The velocity of emitted photoelectrons will be
questions.explanation: $E_{photon}=\dfrac{1240}{300}\approx4.13$ eV; $KE_{max}=4.13-1=3.13$ eV; $v=\sqrt{2KE/m}\approx1\times10^6$ ms$^{-1}$.

questions.q: A proton moving with a momentum P$_1$ has a kinetic energy $\dfrac{1}{8}$th of its rest mass energy. Another light photon having energy equal to the kinetic energy of the proton possesses a momentum P$_2$. Then the ratio $\dfrac{P_1-P_2}{P_1}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Using $KE=\dfrac{P_1^2}{2m}=\dfrac{mc^2}{8}\Rightarrow P_1=\dfrac{mc}{2}$. Photon momentum $P_2=\dfrac{KE}{c}=\dfrac{mc}{8}$. $\dfrac{P_1-P_2}{P_1}=\dfrac{mc/2-mc/8}{mc/2}=\dfrac34$.

questions.q: According to Einstein's photoelectric equation the graph between kinetic energy of photoelectrons ejected and the frequency of incident radiation is: (A) a line of negative slope crossing the frequency axis, (B) a line of positive slope through the origin, (C) a line of positive slope with a positive KE-intercept, (D) a line of positive slope with a positive frequency-intercept (KE = 0 at the threshold frequency, then rises).
questions.explanation: Einstein's equation $KE=hf-\phi_0$ gives a straight line of slope h with KE = 0 at the threshold frequency $f_0=\phi_0/h$, matching graph (D).

questions.q: A light beam of intensity 20 W/cm$^2$ is incident normally on a perfectly reflecting surface of sides 25 cm $\times$ 15 cm. The momentum imparted to the surface by the light per second is
questions.explanation: Power $=20\times375=7500$ W; for perfect reflection, force (momentum/sec) $=\dfrac{2P}{c}=\dfrac{2\times7500}{3\times10^8}=5\times10^{-5}$ kg ms$^{-1}$.

questions.q: The following graph represents the variation of photo current with anode potential for a metal surface. Here $I_1$, $I_2$ and $I_3$ represent intensities and $\gamma_1$, $\gamma_2$, $\gamma_3$ represent frequency for curves 1, 2 and 3 respectively [curves 1 and 2 share the same stopping potential while curve 3 has a different, larger stopping potential; curves 2 and 3 saturate at a higher current than curve 1], then
questions.explanation: Curves 1 and 2 have the same stopping potential, so the incident frequency is the same ($\gamma_1=\gamma_2$), but they saturate at different photocurrents, so their intensities differ ($I_1\ne I_2$).

questions.q: A hot filament liberates an electron with zero initial velocity. The anode potential is 1200 V. The speed of the electron when it strikes the anode is
questions.explanation: $eV=\tfrac12mv^2 \Rightarrow v=\sqrt{2eV/m}=\sqrt{2(1.6\times10^{-19})(1200)/9.11\times10^{-31}}\approx2.1\times10^7$ ms$^{-1}$.

questions.q: An electron is moving with an initial velocity $\vec V = V_0\hat i$ and is in a uniform magnetic field $\vec B = B_0\hat j$. Then its de Broglie wavelength
questions.explanation: Since $\vec v \perp \vec B$, the magnetic force only changes direction, not speed, keeping the electron's speed (and hence its de Broglie wavelength $h/mv$) constant.

questions.q: Light of certain frequency and intensity incident on a photosensitive material causes photoelectric effect. If both the frequency and intensity are doubled, the photoelectric saturation current becomes
questions.explanation: Saturation current depends only on the intensity (number of photons per second) and not on frequency, so doubling the intensity doubles the saturation current.

questions.q: The number of photons falling per second on a completely darkened plate to produce a force of 6.62 × 10$^{-5}$ N is 'n'. If the wavelength of the light falling is 5 × 10$^{-7}$ m, then n = ____ × 10$^{22}$. (h = 6.62 × 10$^{-34}$ J-s)
questions.explanation: Force F = n(h/$\lambda$) since the plate absorbs all photons; n = F$\lambda$/h = (6.62×10$^{-5}$ × 5×10$^{-7}$)/(6.62×10$^{-34}$) = 5×10$^{22}$.

questions.q: The maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons depends on
options: Number of photons in the incident radiation
questions.explanation: By Einstein's photoelectric equation, KE$_{max}$ = h$\nu$ − $\phi$, which depends only on the frequency of the incident radiation (for a given metal).

questions.q: A proton and an $\alpha$ particle are accelerated through the same potential difference V. The ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths is
questions.explanation: $\lambda$ = h/$\sqrt{2mqV}$, so $\lambda_p$/$\lambda_\alpha$ = $\sqrt{(m_\alpha q_\alpha)/(m_p q_p)}$ = $\sqrt{(4×2)/1}$ = $\sqrt{8}$ = 2$\sqrt{2}$.

questions.q: From the following graph of photo current against collector plate potential, for two different intensities of light I$_1$ and I$_2$ [both curves rise from the same negative stopping potential $-V_0$ and saturate at different photocurrent levels, with I$_2$ saturating higher than I$_1$], one can conclude
questions.explanation: Saturation photocurrent is proportional to the intensity of incident light; since the same stopping potential applies to both (same frequency), the graph directly shows I$_1$ < I$_2$.

questions.q: A particle is dropped from a height 'H'. The de Broglie wavelength of the particle depends on height as
questions.explanation: Speed after falling height H is $v=\sqrt{2gH}$. de Broglie wavelength $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv} \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt H} = H^{-1/2}$.

questions.q: The de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated to a potential of 400 V is approximately
questions.explanation: $\lambda=\dfrac{1.227}{\sqrt V}$ nm $=\dfrac{1.227}{\sqrt{400}}=\dfrac{1.227}{20}\approx0.06$ nm.

questions.q: Light of two different frequencies whose photons have energies 1 eV and 2.5 eV respectively, successively illuminate a metallic surface whose work function is 0.5 eV. Ratio of maximum speeds of emitted electrons will be
questions.explanation: $KE_1=1-0.5=0.5$ eV, $KE_2=2.5-0.5=2$ eV; since $v\propto\sqrt{KE}$, ratio $=\sqrt{0.5}:\sqrt{2}=1:2$.

questions.q: Find the de-Broglie wavelength of an electron with kinetic energy of 120 eV.
questions.explanation: $\lambda=\dfrac{1.227}{\sqrt{E(\text{eV})}}$ nm $=\dfrac{1.227}{\sqrt{120}}\approx0.112$ nm $=112$ pm.

questions.q: What is the de Broglie wavelength of the electron accelerated through a potential difference of 100 Volt?
The maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons depends only on
questions.explanation: By Einstein's photoelectric equation, KE$_{max}$ = h$\nu$ - $\phi$, which depends only on the frequency of incident light (for a given metal).

questions.q: Light emitted during the deexcitation of electron from n = 3 to n = 2, when incident on a metal, photoelectrons are just emitted from that metal. In which of the following deexcitations photoelectric effect is not possible ?
questions.explanation: The $n=3\to2$ photon energy ($\approx1.89$ eV for hydrogen) just equals the metal's work function. Checking each transition's energy (10.2 eV, 12.09 eV, 2.86 eV, 0.66 eV), only $n=4\to3$ (0.66 eV) is less than the work function, so photoelectric emission is not possible for it.

questions.q: The additional energy that should be given to an electron to reduce its de-Broglie wavelength from 1 nm to 0.5 nm is
questions.explanation: $KE=h^2/2m\lambda^2\propto1/\lambda^2$. Halving $\lambda$ quadruples $KE$, so the additional energy needed $=4KE-KE=3\times$(initial $KE$).

questions.q: Maximum velocity of the photoelectron emitted by a metal is 1.8 $\times$ 10$^6$ ms$^{-1}$. Take the value of specific charge of the electron is 1.8 $\times$ 10$^{11}$ C kg$^{-1}$. Then the stopping potential in volt is
questions.explanation: $eV_0=\dfrac12mv^2\Rightarrow V_0=\dfrac12\left(\dfrac{m}{e}\right)v^2=\dfrac12\times\dfrac{1}{1.8\times10^{11}}\times(1.8\times10^6)^2=9$ V.

questions.q: $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ are used to illuminate the slits. $\beta_1$ and $\beta_2$ are the corresponding fringe widths. The wavelength $\lambda_1$ can produce photoelectric effect when incident on a metal. But the wavelength $\lambda_2$ cannot produce photoelectric effect. The correct relation between $\beta_1$ and $\beta_2$ is
questions.explanation: Since $\lambda_1$ causes photoemission, it has the higher photon energy and hence the shorter wavelength. Fringe width $\beta=\lambda D/d\propto\lambda$, so the shorter $\lambda_1$ gives the smaller fringe width: $\beta_1<\beta_2$.

questions.q: A proton and an alpha particle are accelerated under the same potential difference. The ratio of de-Broglie wavelengths of the proton and the alpha particle is
questions.explanation: $\lambda=h/\sqrt{2mqV}$, so $\lambda_p/\lambda_\alpha=\sqrt{(m_\alpha q_\alpha)/(m_p q_p)}=\sqrt{(4m_p\cdot2e)/(m_p\cdot e)}=\sqrt8$.

questions.q: 'n' photons of wavelength '$\lambda$' are absorbed by a black body of mass 'm'. The momentum gained by the body is
questions.explanation: Each photon carries momentum $h/\lambda$, and since a black body absorbs (does not reflect) radiation, the body gains this momentum from every photon: total momentum = $nh/\lambda$.

questions.q: The photoelectric threshold wavelength for silver is $\lambda_0$. The energy of the electron ejected from the surface of silver by an incident wavelength $\lambda(\lambda<\lambda_0)$ will be .................
questions.explanation: KE $=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}-\dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0}=hc\left(\dfrac{\lambda_0-\lambda}{\lambda\lambda_0}\right)$.

questions.q: An electron of mass $m_e$ and a proton of mass $m_p$ are moving with the same speed. The ratio of their de-Broglie's wavelengths $\lambda_e/\lambda_p$ is .............
questions.explanation: $\lambda=h/(mv)$, so at the same speed $\lambda_e/\lambda_p=m_p/m_e=1836$.

questions.q: According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the graph of K.E. of the photoelectron emitted from the metal versus the frequency of the incident radiation gives a straight line graph, whose slope .....................
options: is same for all metals and independent of the intensity of the incident radiation.
depends on the nature of the metal.
depends on the intensity of the incident radiation.
depends on the nature of the metal and also on the intensity of incident radiation.
questions.explanation: $KE=h\nu-\phi$; the slope of the $KE$ vs $\nu$ graph is Planck's constant $h$, a universal value independent of the metal or the intensity.

questions.q: G.P. Thomson experimentally confirmed the existence of matter waves by the phenomena
questions.explanation: G.P. Thomson observed electron diffraction rings from a thin metal foil, confirming the wave nature of electrons (de Broglie waves).

questions.q: The kinetic energy of an electron gets tripled, then the de-Broglie wavelength associated with it changes by a factor
questions.explanation: $\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mKE}} \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{KE}}$; tripling KE scales $\lambda$ by a factor $1/\sqrt3$.
